# GitHub Topics

Topics drive discovery on GitHub. Set them under the repo's **About** panel (gear icon → Topics). GitHub allows up to 20 topics; the list below is prioritized so if you can only use 20, take the first 20. All must be lowercase and hyphenated.

## Primary (use these first — highest discoverability)

```text
frontend
frontend-engineering
frontend-development
web-development
javascript
typescript
react
software-architecture
knowledge-base
learning-resources
```text

## Secondary (strong topical relevance)

```text
web-performance
accessibility
design-systems
state-management
testing
software-engineering
best-practices
engineering-decisions
awesome
documentation
```

## Extended (use if slots remain / for niche discovery)

```text
css
html
rendering
ssr
web-platform
progressive-web-app
security
developer-experience
computer-science
trade-offs
```

## Notes on selection

- **`awesome`** and **`learning-resources`** tap into large, actively-browsed topic pages — high inbound traffic for a knowledge base.
- **`engineering-decisions`** and **`trade-offs`** are low-competition but exactly describe the differentiator; they help the right audience find you.
- Framework topics (`react`, `typescript`) are worth the slots because they are among the most-followed topics on GitHub, and the content is genuinely framework-aware.
- Avoid vanity or off-topic tags (e.g. `tutorial`, `beginners`) — they attract mismatched expectations and dilute the signal, contradicting the repository's positioning.
- Keep the **GitHub "About" description** in sync with [`PROJECT_IDENTITY.md`](PROJECT_IDENTITY.md).
